subject: Reliability & SLO comparison follow-up / next tests
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@acme.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Mar 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Reliability & SLO comparison follow-up / next tests

Alex,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps focused on reliability/SLOs so your SRE team can validate: 

Recap from call:
- Primary concern: consistent availability and predictable behavior under burst and partial-region failure (multi-region failover).
- Acme wants an apples-to-apples comparison vs hyperscaler-managed inference endpoints and an objective test plan.
- Procurement and SRE will want: uptime SLA language, rate limits/concurrency guarantees, error budget calculations, and failover timelines.

Redwood quick differentiators (high level):
- Dedicated vs Hosted: Dedicated capacity includes an SLA (99.95% monthly uptime) and isolation for error budgets; hosted API is high-availability but not a contract-backed SLA for trial customers.
- Rate limits: we can provision per-deal concurrency and token throughput limits on Dedicated; hosted tiers have default shared limits but we can increase bursts based on commit.
- Failover behavior: multi-region routing with automated failover in ~30-90s depending on session state and KV cache priming; we provide safe fallback to smaller compatible model variants to preserve latency during degradation.
- Observability: token-level latency, per-route error rates, and trace hooks for root-cause analysis are included; audit logs and retention are available for Private/Dedicated deployments.

Proposed test plan (short):
1) Throughput test: 1k concurrent requests, 20k tokens/sec sustained for 30 minutes against your sample workload.
2) Error-budget exercise: inject transient errors (5-10% synthetic errors) and verify 95th/99th latency and effective error budget consumption.
3) Region-failure drill: simulate a regional outage and measure failover completion and session consistency.

Attachments: product_slo_table.xlsx (SLO summary), mutual_action_plan.pdf (timeline + owners).

Next steps:
- If this looks right, can you loop in the SRE contact who will run the tests?
- We'll share a runnable test plan (redwood_test_plan.yaml) and a DocuSign link for the Dedicated trial SLA if you want to move forward.

I'm copying Marissa (solutions) and Rishi (reliability) on the follow-up.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

- For rate limits: does Redwood guarantee per-tenant concurrency for Dedicated (hard cap we can rely on), or is it a soft limit with throttling?
- Region failover: concrete expected RTO (how long session-state rehydration + KV cache repop takes). Hyperscaler teams typically claim <60s, can you give a more specific number or a range?

Looping in Jamie (SRE) to coordinate the test execution. Jamie, can you share preferred windows for a throughput run next week and whether you want us to run the error-injection from our side or have Redwood trigger it?

Appreciate the attachments, will review.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Mar 2026 13:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reliability & SLO comparison follow-up / next tests

Alex / Jamie,

Thanks — answering the specific questions inline and attaching a lightweight runnable test plan: redwood_test_plan.yaml. 

SLA credits and language:
- Dedicated SLA: 99.95% monthly uptime. Credit model: for each 0.1% below 99.95% we return X% of the monthly Dedicated fee (we'll include exact contract language in DocuSign). I've added a sample SLA clause to the mutual_action_plan.pdf.

Rate limits / concurrency guarantees:
- Dedicated: hard per-tenant concurrency cap can be provisioned as part of the Dedicated pool config. In practice we'll provision a capacity pool to meet your target sustained throughput (example: 1k concurrent requests, 20k tokens/sec).
- Hosted: soft limits with throttling; we can pre-warm and increase burst capacity for demos but it's not the same as Dedicated isolation.

Failover / RTO:
- Expected failover completion: typically 30-90s depending on cache warm-up and session size. For stateless workloads you'll typically see sub-30s failover to another region; for stateful sessions with large KV caches expect toward the upper end.
- We provide a fallback model variant option: when a primary model pool is degraded we can automatically route to a compatible, lower-memory variant to preserve availability while degrading quality gracefully.

Error budget calculation (example):
- SLA 99.95% => allowed downtime ~21.6 minutes/month. We treat sustained service errors (5xx or timeouts) and platform outages as SLA-impacting events; transient/request-level retries that succeed within configured client timeouts are not charged to SLA.

Test coordination:
- Suggested windows: Tue/Wed next week 09:00-13:00 PT for throughput (less noisy background traffic).
- We can run the error-injection from our env or you can trigger it; recommend you trigger it so you see how your orchestration responds.

Attachments included: redwood_test_plan.yaml (runnable), product_slo_table.xlsx, mutual_action_plan.pdf. I've also started the DocuSign envelope for a Dedicated trial SLA in case procurement is ready: https://docusign.com/ACME-Redwood-SLA-2026

Marissa / Rishi: can you confirm resource availability on our side and whether we want to have an on-call engineer during the exercise?

Ben

Ben / Alex,

Thanks for the plan. We can do Wed 2026-04-01 09:00-12:00 PT for the throughput test. We'll run the error-injection from our side (we prefer to control the failure window). A couple of follow-ups from SRE: 

- Can you confirm RBAC and audit-log retention options for Dedicated (we need 12 months minimum for logs).
- For the region-failure drill, please include the exact steps you'll take to route traffic (DNS swap, LB updates, or internal router failover) so we can sync our traffic-shifting plan.
- Also please point us to the DocuSign package and the exact SLA wording for the credit table so procurement can review.

One last ask: can Redwood provide a short JSON/CSV export of the per-request error/log samples from the throughput run (we'll post-process for our internal RCA)?

If you can send the DocuSign link and the test artifact export format (small example), we'll confirm the window and owners.

Jamie Lee
SRE Lead, Platform Reliability | Acme AI
jamie.lee@acme.ai
